gaps.sentence: She had her laptop ___ (repair) after the coffee spill.
gaps.explanation: Causative structure: had + her laptop + repaired. A technician performed the repair.

gaps.sentence: The debt ___ (repay) in full by May, he promised.
gaps.explanation: Reported future passive: would be + past participle after a past reporting verb.

gaps.sentence: The new stadium ___ by the end of the decade.
gaps.explanation: 'By the end of the decade' needs future perfect passive: will have been + completed. The stadium is completed by somebody.

gaps.sentence: The invitation ___ (send) to the wrong address — nobody on this street received one.
gaps.explanation: Perfect modal passive: must have been + sent. The evidence forces the conclusion.

gaps.sentence: My usual barber's chair ___ (fix), so I'm trying a new salon.
gaps.explanation: Present continuous passive: is being + fixed for an unfinished, ongoing repair.

gaps.sentence: The report must ___ before Friday's board meeting.
gaps.explanation: Modal passive: must be + submitted. 'Been' would require have (must have been submitted).

gaps.sentence: They're getting the garden ___ (landscape) this spring.
gaps.explanation: Causative with get: are getting + the garden + landscaped.
Past simple passive: was + demolished. The demolition company is not mentioned.
